activities.title: 2. Match Collocations and Phrases
activities.instruction: Match the words or phrases in A with those in B to form environmental partnerships.

activities.title: 3. Odd Word Out
activities.instruction: Identify the word that does not belong in each semantic group.

items.reason: 'male' is a gender term, while the others are animal species.
'species' refers to biological kinds of animals/plants, while the others are types of trash.
'starfish' is a living sea creature, while the others are water and ocean features.
'pollute' means to damage the earth, whereas save, protect, and clean mean conserving it.

activities.title: 4. Match Synonyms
activities.instruction: Match each word on the left with its closest synonym on the right.

activities.title: 5. Complete with the Correct Verbs
activities.instruction: Fill in each sentence using the verbs: dump, weigh, breathe, recycle, grow, lay, protect.

items.text: People should ______ endangered animals.
If the air is polluted, people cannot ______.
We must all try to ______ all the paper that we do not use in schools any more.
Factories should not ______ their waste in rivers.
Caretta-caretta turtles ______ eggs in the sand.
Monk seals grow to about 2.40 m in length and ______ up to 320 kg.
Sulphur dioxide makes plants and trees ______ more slowly.

activities.title: 6. Word Derivatives & Formations
activities.instruction: Complete each sentence with a derivative of the base word in brackets.

items.text: The boy was out of ______ (BREATHE) and it was obvious that he was tired.
items.hint: noun form: the air in your lungs

items.text: Monk seals are very heavy. Their ______ (WEIGH) is around 320 kg.
Carbon Monoxide is a dangerous ______ (POLLUTE).
Many companies are not careful about how they get rid of their ______ (INDUSTRY) waste.
Caretta-caretta and Monachus-monachus are ______ (DANGER) animals.
Sophia is a member of the ______ (ENVIRONMENT) team in her school.

activities.title: 1. Visiting the Parents' Village (Past Perfect)
activities.instruction: Complete the sentences using the Past Perfect (had + V3) to show what had changed before you returned.

items.text: The tree outside the house was not there. People ______ (cut) it down.
The bridge over the stream was not there. It ______ (fall) down.
The small lake near the village was not clean. People ______ (throw) their rubbish in.
The storks that used to live there ______ (fly) away.
My grandfather no longer had his donkey. He ______ (sell) it.

activities.title: 2. What Had Happened in Greenville?
activities.instruction: Read the poem about Greenville turning brown. Write what had happened before Mr. Green returned.
model_answers: People had cut down the green trees.
Factories had dumped toxic waste into the clean river.
Cars and power plants had polluted the crystal blue sky.
checklist: Explain changes to air, trees, or water.
Reflect the poem's themes of smog and pollution.

activities.title: 3. Combine Sentences with Past Perfect
activities.instruction: Join the two events using the connector in brackets and the Past Perfect for the earlier event.

items.text: Mark was sad. Some companies dumped toxic waste on the beach. (because) → Mark was sad because some companies ______ toxic waste on the beach.
The tide washed up the starfish. Mark arrived. (when) → The tide ______ the starfish when Mark arrived.
items.hint: tide washed up before Mark arrived

items.text: The bears left. People took over their natural habitat. (because) → The bears left because people ______ over their natural habitat.
The dog was in hospital. He broke his leg. (because) → The dog was in hospital because he ______ his leg.
The birds left the stream. Factories dumped waste there. (after) → The birds left the stream after factories ______ waste there.

activities.title: 4. Past Simple or Past Perfect?
activities.instruction: Put the verbs in brackets into the correct tense (Past Simple or Past Perfect Simple).

items.text: The wolf ______ (attack) the hunter after he ______ (try) to kill him.
The fisherman ______ (kill) the seal because it ______ (destroy) his nets.
When Tom ______ (arrive) at the sea, he could not swim because people ______ (throw) bottles in.
Maria ______ (leave) the beach when the tsunami ______ (hit) her island.
The boy ______ (throw) the starfish into the sea after the tide ______ (wash) them out.

activities.title: 5. Helen's Beach Checklist (Had / Hadn't)
activities.instruction: Look at what Helen checked off before leaving the beach. Complete the sentences with had or hadn't.

items.text: She ______ (collect) plastic bags. [Checked]
She ______ (take) her suntan oil. [Unchecked]
She ______ (put) her tennis racket in her bag. [Unchecked]
She ______ (put) the towel in her bag. [Checked]
She ______ (throw) empty cans in the recycling bin. [Checked]
She ______ (pick up) colourful pebbles. [Checked]

activities.title: 6. Because or Because Of?
activities.instruction: Choose 'because' (followed by subject + verb) or 'because of' (followed by noun phrase).

items.text: He could not stay any longer ______ the awful smell.
items.hint: followed by noun phrase 'the awful smell'

items.text: Tim was surprised to see such a bird in his garden ______ he had not seen any for many years!
items.hint: followed by clause 'he had not seen'

items.text: The cat was at the vet ______ she had had a car accident.
The citizens felt awful ______ the smog.

activities.title: 7. Reason and Result Matching
activities.instruction: Match each environmental cause/reason with its corresponding effect/result.

pairs.colA: People play games on the beach
pairs.colB: a lot of turtle eggs break
pairs.phrase: People play games → turtle eggs break

pairs.colA: Black smoke comes out of chimneys
Acid rain falls on the valley

activities.title: 8. Connectors: So, As a result, Because, Because of
activities.instruction: Complete each sentence with the appropriate reason or result connector.

items.text: The water was not clean, ______ the fisherman did not want to fish.
The bear could not find food to eat, and ______, she feels very hungry today.
The pigeons could not find a place to build their nest ______ people had cut down all the trees.
The tourists did not want to swim ______ the polluted water.

activities.title: 9. Guided Writing: Advice Email to Shalleen
activities.instruction: Write an email to your Australian friend Shalleen explaining why she should choose a quiet, eco-friendly beach instead of a crowded, polluted tourist resort.
activities.model_text:
Hello Shalleen,
I was glad to hear that you want to visit Greece this summer! The island you are thinking of visiting is very famous, but when I was there last year, I could not swim because of the thick yacht oil and crowds of noisy motorboats. The beach was polluted with plastic cups, and the turtles could not nest. I really think you should visit a quiet island with protected nature reserves instead!
Best wishes,
Maria
checklist: Explain why swimming was difficult (oil, noise, trash).
Use 'because of' with a noun phrase.

activities.title: 1. The Secret of Bog Creek
activities.instruction: Read the story of Bob and Jeannie at Bog Creek and answer the comprehension questions.

questions.sample: Bog Creek is a freshwater stream in New Jersey.

questions.q: What was the secret of Bog Creek?
accepted: Some people used the farm as a place to dump their old chemicals and paints.
People dumped chemicals and paints there.
Secret dumping of toxic chemicals and paints.
questions.sample: People used the farm as a secret place to dump old chemicals and paint waste.
